```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Stops an EC2 instance.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$'
  KeyName:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,255}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: StopInstance
    action: aws:changeInstanceState
    inputs:
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      DesiredState: stopped
```", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "cd66dce3-e59e-467d-8589-af0a1b36b1e4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The runbook is syntactically valid and the `aws:changeInstanceState` inputs are correct, so it should work. I'd fix one issue before release and make a few small improvements. I reviewed it by reading it. I haven't run it or validated it against the SSM API.

## Fix before release
- **`KeyName` is unused.** No step references `{{KeyName}}`. It has no default, so every caller must supply a value that does nothing. That is confusing, and it breaks automation that doesn't pass it. It looks left over from a copy/paste, so remove it.

## Recommended improvements
- **No step timeout or failure handling.** Add `timeoutSeconds` and `onFailure: Abort`, so a stuck stop doesn't run until the default timeout.
- **No parameter descriptions.** Add them so operators know what to pass, especially for `AutomationAssumeRole`.
- **Use a native instance ID type.** `AWS::EC2::Instance::Id` validates the ID in the console and in API calls. It also gives console users an instance picker. Your regex is valid, so this is optional.
- **Document the permissions.** The assume role needs `ec2:StopInstances` and `ec2:DescribeInstances`. It also needs `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`, because the step polls for the stopped state. Scope the role to the specific instances or to a tag condition where you can.

## Operational notes
- The step is idempotent. Running it on an already-stopped instance succeeds.
- Stopping an instance in an Auto Scaling group will cause the group to treat it as unhealthy and replace it. Suspend the group's processes first if that matters.
- Stopping an instance clears instance store data. It also releases a non-Elastic public IP.
- `Force` is not set, so the stop is a normal graceful shutdown. That is usually what you want.

## Suggested revision
```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Stops an EC2 instance and waits until it reaches the stopped state.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
    description: (Required) IAM role Automation assumes. Needs ec2:StopInstances, ec2:DescribeInstances and ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus.
  InstanceId:
    type: AWS::EC2::Instance::Id
    description: (Required) ID of the EC2 instance to stop.
mainSteps:
  - name: StopInstance
    action: aws:changeInstanceState
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      DesiredState: stopped
```

If `KeyName` is intentionally part of a shared parameter contract, for example because other runbooks or a pipeline pass it, keep it but add a default and a description saying it's unused. Otherwise remove it.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
